_note: The parts of speech to look up (/grammar/parts-of-speech) and Regi's line under the part-of-speech label of the flashcards (wortschatz-app.js). `practice` = the anchor of the exercise on /parts-of-speech where the class comes up. `fehler` = the word pair on /grammar/common-mistakes that belongs to the class; linked to the Italian pairs of the idioms-mistakes item. `id` = the pos field in the lexicon; the article has no lexicon word of its own but belongs here. `examples` are set by hand (Italian, A1) so the page does not depend on the lexicon. `say` is the short form for the card (≤ 8 words), `what` the sentence on the page, `tr` its translation into the help languages (`en` = the same sentence; the ar/uk/tr drafts of the Spanish course were removed where `what` changed for Italian, and only `en` is kept).

classes.name: Noun
classes.say: A noun is a name for something.
classes.what: A noun is a name: for a person, an animal, a thing or an idea.
classes.tip: Every Italian noun is masculine or feminine: il libro, la casa. Most nouns have a plural: libro – libri. Names of people and places start with a capital letter: Amina, Roma. Days and months do not: lunedì, maggio.

learn.label: Nouns and gender: rule and exercises

tr.en: A noun is a name: for a person, an animal, a thing or an idea.

classes.name: Article
classes.say: An article comes before a noun.
classes.what: An article comes before a noun and agrees with it: il, lo, la, l', i, gli, le for a thing we both know; un, uno, una, un' for one of many, or some.
classes.ask: il or la? un or una?
classes.tip: The article shows the gender and the number: il libro, la casa, i libri, le case. The form depends on the first sound: lo zaino, gli studenti, l'amico. a + il becomes al, di + il becomes del: vado al bar, vengo dal medico.

learn.label: Articles: il, lo, la, un, una – rule and exercises

tr.en: An article comes before a noun and agrees with it: il, lo, la, l', i, gli, le for a thing we both know; un, uno, una, un' for one of many, or some.

classes.name: Verb
classes.say: A verb says what someone does.

sub.name: pronominal verb
sub.what: A verb that comes with a pronoun: mi alzo, ti ricordi, si sposa.

classes.what: A verb says what someone does or what happens.
classes.ask: What does he do? What happens?
classes.tip: The ending shows the person, so the pronoun is usually left out: parlo, parli, parla. The infinitive ends in -are, -ere or -ire: parlare, vedere, dormire.

tr.en: A verb says what someone does or what happens.

classes.name: Adjective
classes.say: An adjective says what something is like.
classes.what: An adjective says what someone or something is like.
classes.tip: An adjective agrees with its noun and usually goes after it: una casa bianca, i libri nuovi. Some have one form for both genders: un appartamento grande, una casa grande.

tr.en: An adjective says what someone or something is like.

classes.name: Adverb
classes.say: An adverb says when, where or how.
classes.what: An adverb says when, where or how something happens.
classes.tip: Adverbs don't change their form. Many end in -mente: rapidamente, normalmente. Others don't: oggi, qui, sempre, bene.

tr.en: An adverb says when, where or how something happens.

classes.name: Pronoun
classes.say: A pronoun stands for a noun.
classes.what: A pronoun stands for a noun, so you don't have to repeat it.
classes.tip: Anna arriva tardi. → Lei arriva tardi, or just: Arriva tardi. Vedo Anna. → La vedo.

tr.en: A pronoun stands for a noun, so you don't have to repeat it.

classes.name: Preposition
classes.say: A preposition comes before a noun: a, in, di.
classes.what: A preposition comes before a noun and shows place, time or direction.
classes.tip: After a preposition, use a noun, a pronoun or an infinitive: con il mio amico, per te, prima di uscire. Many join with the article: di + la = della, in + il = nel.

tr.en: A preposition comes before a noun and shows place, time or direction.

classes.name: Conjunction
classes.say: A conjunction joins words and sentences.
classes.what: A conjunction joins words or sentences.
classes.tip: e, o and ma join two sentences: Sono stanco, ma vengo. perché gives a reason. e becomes ed before e-: Mario ed Elena.

tr.en: A conjunction joins words or sentences.

classes.name: Number
classes.what: A number word says how much or how many, or in which position.
classes.ask: How many? How much? Which one in order?
classes.tip: due bambini (how many?), il secondo giorno (which one in order?). uno becomes un before a masculine noun: un libro, ventun anni.

tr.en: A number word says how much or how many, or in which position.

classes.name: Phrase
classes.also: not a part of speech, a fixed group of words
classes.say: A phrase: several words, one meaning.
classes.what: A phrase is several words that together have one fixed meaning.
classes.tip: Learn it as a whole. Translated word for word, it often doesn't work: In bocca al lupo! Come va?

tr.en: A phrase is several words that together have one fixed meaning.
